program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 2000

source_provenance: Sider Scholar + NCBI PubMed exact-source verification
repository-wide PMID collision screening against prior enrichment waves and active Waves 1501-1925

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 2000

waves.focus: New Jersey poison-center outbreak identified 34 patients with severe toxicity after tianeptine products; product testing found variable composition including synthetic cannabinoids, kava alkaloids and cannabinoids, and many patients required intubation/ICU care.

Online survey found tianeptine use uncommon within a gray-market-product sample but frequently associated with rapid tolerance, adverse effects, severe past-year SUD criteria and strong perceived addictiveness/overdose risk; self-selected sample limits prevalence inference.

Case report describes concomitant tianeptine and alcohol use disorders treated with buprenorphine-naloxone; single-patient management evidence supports clinical awareness without establishing an optimal protocol.

Case report and review describes severe tianeptine use disorder with psychiatric deterioration, dependence and withdrawal, emphasizing diagnostic barriers and need for addiction-treatment referral; case-level evidence only.

Systematic review of 25 studies found frequent habitual misuse, overdose, withdrawal and co-use, with naloxone and buprenorphine appearing in reported management; underlying literature is largely case-based and heterogeneous.

Three-case series and review describes rapid tolerance, opioid-like intoxication/withdrawal and use of naloxone, buprenorphine, clonidine and supportive care; treatment conclusions remain limited by case evidence.

Systematic review of 53 publications found opioid-like dependence, withdrawal and overdose, with substantial ICU use in retrospective series and reported fatalities among detailed overdose cases; evidence is dominated by case reports/series.

Case report describes severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, encephalopathy and pulmonary infiltrates after combined kratom/tianeptine ingestion, improving with naloxone and ICU supportive care; co-exposure prevents single-agent attribution.

NLP-assisted qualitative analysis of Reddit posts found increasing discussion of tianeptine dependence, withdrawal and co-ingestion; useful real-world signal but self-reported social-media content cannot estimate clinical incidence.

Survey of addiction-conference clinicians found substantial knowledge gaps around kratom, phenibut and tianeptine despite high concern and support for more research/regulation; clinician-practice context rather than toxicity incidence.

Case report describes sustained abstinence from tianeptine after methadone treatment when high-dose buprenorphine had not controlled cravings/withdrawal; illustrates a treatment gap but cannot establish comparative efficacy.

Laboratory analysis found none of 12 US sports supplements labeled with Eria jarensis were accurately labeled; several contained undeclared stimulants, including FDA-prohibited DMAA, and caffeine content varied dramatically.

Review summarizes laboratory risk-mitigation approaches for dietary-supplement adulteration, including identity/purity testing, supplier quality agreements and third-party verification; quality-system evidence rather than clinical efficacy.

Review of authentication methods for botanicals in plant extracts and supplements highlights identity testing as a core defense against substitution and adulteration; methodological quality-control evidence.
Review documents the problem of sports supplements adulterated with anabolic steroids and the anti-doping/health consequences of undeclared exposure; product-quality and harm-reduction evidence.

US market analysis found wide deviations in Rhodiola rosavin/salidroside content, probable undisclosed synthetic salidroside in one product and trace metals in tested products; strong formulation/authenticity warning.
Analytical study applies LC-MS/MS and LC-QTOF/MS screening for anabolic-androgenic steroids in illicit dietary supplements/counterfeit drugs; useful adulterant-detection and quality-control evidence.
Post-market analysis of 65 online Cordyceps products found more than half falsified, 11% unregistered and 6.2% adulterated with corticosteroids, alongside frequent illegal disease claims.
Validated GC-MS method targets undeclared diuretics in adulterated weight-loss supplements, supporting forensic/product-quality surveillance rather than efficacy claims.
Analysis of 23 green-coffee-bean supplements found wide chlorogenic-acid/caffeine variability, products labeled 50% CGAs with none detected, and decaffeinated products exceeding caffeine thresholds.

Analytical chemistry study isolated previously unreported tadalafil analogues illegally added to a male sexual herbal supplement, demonstrating pharmaceutical adulteration of purportedly herbal products.
Toxicovigilance report documents multiple batches of a slimming supplement adulterated with sibutramine and associated clinical cases; high-value undeclared-drug safety signal.

Case report describes yellow-oleander toxicity from a misrepresented dietary supplement, underscoring that botanical/product identity failures can cause severe poisoning independent of labeled intent.

Case report attributes drug-induced liver injury to a turmeric supplement containing piperine after competing causes were evaluated; single-case evidence supports hepatotoxicity vigilance, especially with bioavailability-enhancing formulations.

Safety review focuses on reproductive, thyroid and immune-system concerns relevant to ashwagandha use as a food/additive, emphasizing unresolved risk questions and the need for population-specific caution.
